source.title: Exploring Data Scaling Trends and Effects in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
source.authors: Wei Shen; Guan-Lin Liu; Zheng Wu; Ruo-Fei Zhu; Qingping Yang; Chao Xin; Yu Yue; Lin Yan

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies prompt-data and model-size effects during RLHF, not held-out pretraining loss or the claimed pretraining scaling laws. Its RLHF benchmark results do not test whether pretraining loss follows power laws or whether smaller-run fits predict larger runs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports RLHF prompt-data scaling and a qualitative positive trend with model size, but it does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, fit power laws, test extrapolation, or evaluate a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. It also reports reward-model, response-entropy, and task-benchmark results that do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study examines RLHF prompt selection and training schedules (Pre-PPO, early math/code emphasis) on ~25B and ~150B models, scored on internal benchmarks. It measures no pretraining loss, fits no power law, tests no extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation, and does not relate downstream performance to scale or loss in a predictive form. Its 'scaling' results are about prompt quantity and a two-point model-size comparison of method gains, not the claim's versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that reward hacking and declining response diversity are the bottlenecks to RLHF data scaling. They find that Pre-PPO selection of hard, low-reward prompts and early emphasis on math and coding improve performance on both model sizes. RTV resists reward hacking best, followed by GenRM with ground truth. Simply adding more prompts does not help.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies RLHF prompt construction and training schedules rather than the original pretraining-loss scaling-law method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that increasing newly collected prompt volume within Pre-PPO from 10% to 20% or 50% degrades overall RLHF performance; it also reports results varying by task and reward-model supervision.

fits_no_version.finding: In RLHF, adding many more prompts did not improve performance: 6M prompts showed no gain over 1M (Fig. 2). Within Pre-PPO, raising the newly collected prompt share from 10% to 20% or 50% degraded overall performance (Fig. 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RLHF performance does not scale monotonically with prompt quantity; prompt quality and curation limit data scaling in RLHF.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), as stated in the supplied metadata
record.problems: The data-volume results in Figure 8 are presented only graphically, without numerical values or uncertainty in the text. The paper's model-size trend is qualitative and is not a fitted scaling law.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for downstream benchmark scores, reward-model scores, or response entropy: these do not measure any of the listed claim versions, and are not additional results on the RLHF prompt-volume scaling finding.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in other regimes. RLHF data scaling is studied, but no power-law form is fitted.
Predictable downstream improvement with scale or loss. There are only two model sizes, and the comparison is of method gains, not a scale trend.
How fitted exponents and the compute-optimal split depend on fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The word 'scaling' in the title refers to RLHF prompt data, not pretraining scaling laws. The model-size 'positive scaling trend' only means the method's gains persist at ~150B (Tables 1 and 3). It is not a scaling-law test.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law fit and range.
Prediction of larger-run pretraining loss from fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Architecture-shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; RLHF prompt quantity results do not test a power-law loss form.
The study reports downstream task evaluations, but does not test whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.
